questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

The diagram shows a production possibility curve for an economy that produces only two goods, X and Y. good Y 500 0 500 1000 1500 2000 good X The economy produces 400 of good Y and produces on its production possibility curve. Which quantity of good X is given up?

In the recession of 2011 some governments decided to reduce expenditure and decrease the numbers working in the public sector. Trades unions organised a mass demonstration in protest. Which question relating to the government decision is a normative question rather than a positive question?

options.A: How should public sector industries be run?
options.B: What goods and services are produced by the public sector?
options.C: When the government reduced its expenditure what happened to the level of unemployment?
options.D: Why was there a trade union protest?

questions.questionText: The table identifies the functions of money and the principal benefit that each function produces. Which function of money is correctly matched with its principal benefit? function benefit

options.A: medium of exchange permits a system of credit to operate
options.B: standard of deferred payment encourages the accumulation of funds for future use
options.C: store of wealth overcomes the drawbacks of the barter system
options.D: unit of account allows the relative value of goods to be compared

questions.questionText: Which change does not have an immediate effect on the position of the demand curve for a product?

options.A: a fall in the price of a complementary product
options.B: an increase in the labour costs of its production
options.C: a range of new products entering the market
options.D: a rise in the price of a substitute product

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand curve for a product. price D O quantity Which statement is correct?

options.A: Demand is less elastic at higher prices than at lower prices.
options.B: Consumer expenditure on the product always rises when price falls.
options.C: Price elasticity of demand is different at every price.
options.D: Price elasticity of demand equals one at every price.

questions.questionText: Why might a product have a high negative income elasticity of demand and a high price elasticity of demand?

options.A: It is an inferior good with close substitutes.
options.B: It is an inferior good with weak complements.
options.C: It is a normal good with close substitutes.
options.D: It is a normal good with weak complements.

options.A: It is equal to 0.0.

A rise in the price of a good is accompanied by an increase in the quantity demanded. What could explain this?

options.A: Consumers spend a high proportion of disposable income on the good.
options.B: The price of a complementary good has also increased.
options.C: The substitute goods are all very much more expensive.
options.D: The price of the good is taken to be an indication of the level of quality.

questions.questionText: Which statement about a product with external costs must be correct?

options.A: The consumption of the product has positive effects on third parties.
options.B: The private costs of its production exceed the social costs of its production.
options.C: The production of the product has negative effects on third parties.
options.D: The social costs of its production exceed the social benefits of its production.

questions.questionText: The government buys more speed cameras from the manufacturer. What would be included among the external benefits of increasing the number of speed cameras on a country’s roads? additional additional jobs government a reduction in a reduction in fuel in camera revenue from road accidents consumption production fines on motorists

options.A: no no yes yes

questions.questionText: Advances in technology are turning a number of goods which are usually thought of as public goods, for example, television broadcasting, into private goods. Why might this be so?

options.A: Consumer surplus is being increased.
options.B: The costs of production are being reduced.
options.C: It is becoming easier to exclude non-payers.
options.D: The technology is increasing the number of people consuming the goods.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the market for wheat. S P P price 1 D O X Y Z quantity If the government wishes to fix the price at OP what quantity of wheat must the government buy?

options.A: OZ B XY C XZ D YZ

LK is its trading possibility curve which shows possible combinations of good X and good Y after specialising in the product in which it has comparative advantage, and then trading it. L J good X R S O T K good Y The country consumes OR of good X and OT of good Y. Which quantities of goods X and Y does it produce? good X good Y

questions.questionText: A country’s terms of trade increased from the base year value of 100 to 120 in the following year. What changes in export prices and import prices would have caused this? export prices import prices

options.A: decreased 10% increased 10%

questions.questionText: The balance of payments accounts are arranged in the following way. Which total is the current account balance? balance of trade in goods + balance of trade in services =total A + net income = total B + net transfers = total C + capital balance = total D financial balance errors and omissions
A country has a population of 100 million. 60 million are of working age and 50 million are in the labour force. The country’s unemployment rate is 10%. How many people are employed?

options.A: 40 million B 45 million C 50 million D 54 million

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the output of an economy. AS AD price level P AD O Y real GDP What would be the effect of a decrease in net exports? aggregate price level real GDP supply

options.A: shift decrease unchanged

questions.questionText: A country experienced an annual inflation rate of 2% for four successive years. Which statement is correct for the four-year period?

options.A: The price level rose by 8%.
options.B: The price level rose by more than 8%.
options.C: The real value of money rose by 8%.
options.D: The real value of money rose by more than 8%.

questions.questionText: In 2010 it was reported that there were concerns when a government kept interest rates very low despite a threat of inflation. Why might the government’s policy have caused concern at this time?

options.A: Low interest rates encourage increased consumer spending.
options.B: Low interest rates lead to increased spending on capital equipment.
options.C: Low interest rates mean imports will increase.
options.D: Low interest rates will cause an increase in the exchange rate.

questions.questionText: Australia’s spending on imports falls and, at the same time, investment abroad by Australian firms declines. Which diagram shows the immediate effect of these changes on the market for the Australian dollar?

options.A: B

questions.questionText: Which policy, adopted by a government with the intention of reducing the rate of inflation, might cause a greater deficit on the balance of payments?

options.A: higher foreign exchange rates for its currency
options.B: higher interest rates for domestic customers
options.D: higher tax rates on consumer incomes

questions.questionText: What is likely to result in an increase in a country’s balance of payments deficit (disequilibrium) in the short run but may reduce it in the long run?

options.A: an appreciation of the country’s currency
options.B: substantial foreign investment by the country’s residents
options.C: the introduction of controls on capital outflows
